approach: Add three optional lists to the introspection answer and record: other_causes, open_hypotheses and contradictions (Vec<String>, serde default, omitted when empty, so old records parse and keep their bytes). The model is asked for them in SYSTEM_PROMPT and answer_schema. apply_answer puts their entries through the same redaction and boundary-reword pass as the four prose fields, drops blank entries, keeps at most INTROSPECTION_LIST_CAP per list, then stores them. IntrospectionRecord::validate rejects a blank entry or an over-cap list. `cause` stays the one main cause, so hestia counting is untouched. The cleaning step is pulled into a small private fn so its failure path can be tested. The mechanism and a measure ending `status: not shown` go into docs/spec.toml, with a CHANGELOG entry. Because Rust struct literals must name every field, each existing `IntrospectionRecord { .. }` literal in the workspace gets three `Vec::new()` lines; these are compile-forced one-line edits in test or helper code, not behavior changes (see decision 9).

decisions.choice: Three flat Vec<String> fields on IntrospectionRecord, each `#[serde(default, skip_serializing_if = "Vec::is_empty")]`, placed after `cause`.
decisions.reason: Matches the existing pattern for `planning_stopped` and `jev` (introspection.rs:215,221). `deny_unknown_fields` is on the record (introspection.rs:181), so the fields must be declared. Skipping empty lists keeps old records byte-identical; the test at records.rs:1735-1756 asserts `to_json` equals the input bytes.

rejected.option: One nested `doubt` struct or a `Vec<Cause>` with confidence
rejected.why: More shape than the requirement needs. Confidence per cause is OLY-R1-02, not this requirement.

rejected.option: Fold the lists into `cause` as text
rejected.why: `cause` is the grouping key for hestia (hestia.rs:810, 928); joining text would change which mistakes count together.

decisions.choice: Keep `cause` as the main cause and leave hestia, proposals, labeled logic, evidence_labels logic, review and status logic untouched.
decisions.reason: Those read only `cause` (hestia.rs:810,1013; proposals.rs:328; labeled.rs:261; evidence_labels.rs:314; review.rs:199; status.rs:808; status/planning.rs:124). The brief puts changing how hestia counts causes out of scope.

rejected.option: Count other_causes in feedback_dimension_counts or the status view
rejected.why: Out of scope (no `athena status` line). It would also change IntrospectionView JSON that cli tests read.

decisions.choice: Put the new entries into the same `text` vector as the four prose fields (after index 3) so one redact_all scan and one reword pass cover them; split them off before the empty-field check, which stays on the four main fields only.
decisions.reason: Gives the new lists exactly the existing redaction and reword treatment (introspect.rs:1485-1499) with one gitleaks scan. Blank list entries are dropped before this, so a blank entry does not trip `the answer leaves a field empty`.

rejected.option: Redact the lists in a second redact_all call
rejected.why: A second gitleaks run for no gain.

rejected.option: Fail the answer on a blank list entry
rejected.why: A model that returns an empty string in an optional list should not lose a whole introspection.

decisions.choice: Extract `clean_texts(texts, redactor, reword)` from apply_answer. It returns Err with the existing failure messages (`the answer could not be redacted`, `the answer could not be reworded: {why}`). apply_answer passes `plain_boundary_text` as `reword`.
decisions.reason: Reading boundary.rs:209-280 found no input that plain_boundary_text rejects, and the redactor fails only when gitleaks fails (secrets.rs:149-161, binary chosen by the process-wide env var ATHENA_GITLEAKS, secrets.rs:93). A test cannot reach the failure path of apply_answer deterministically. The closure stands in only for the reword step; the loop, the stop at the first refusal and the message are production code.

rejected.option: Set ATHENA_GITLEAKS in a test to a failing stub
rejected.why: The env var is process-wide and tests run in parallel, so other tests that build a Redactor would flake.
Larger change in another crate for one test.

decisions.choice: A boundary word in a new-list entry is reworded and the introspection is recorded, as for the four existing fields. It fails only when redaction or rewording cannot clean the text.
decisions.reason: Criterion 5 says new lists are 'handled like the existing fields'. The existing fields reword and record (introspect.rs:1491-1499, test at 2008-2059). The 'recorded as failed' case applies where cleaning errs, which the clean_texts test covers.

rejected.option: Fail the whole introspection on any boundary word in a list
rejected.why: Differs from the four existing fields and would lose the record for a word that can be reworded.

decisions.choice: Cap each list at INTROSPECTION_LIST_CAP = 5 in the data crate; apply_answer keeps the first 5 and notes the rest with ui.line; validate() rejects more than 5 or a blank entry.
decisions.reason: A bounded record, and the data crate owns what a valid record is. Lists written by this code always pass validate.

rejected.why: A model could write an unbounded list into a committed record.

decisions.choice: Make the three new keys `required` in answer_schema and keep `#[serde(default)]` on Answer.
decisions.reason: The schema is `additionalProperties: false` and `gate` is already required-and-nullable. Required keys make the model state `[]` when there is nothing. serde default keeps fake replies in cli tests (introspection.rs:76-90, retry.rs:95) and old stored answers parsing.

rejected.why: The model may skip the question; an explicit empty list is clearer evidence of 'considered, none'.

decisions.choice: Do not edit docs/records.md or docs/design/defaults-loop.md; document the change in CHANGELOG.md and the spec mechanism.
decisions.reason: Keeps the change to the listed deliverables plus the literals that must compile.

decisions.choice: Answer to findings 3-13 (files outside the deliverables): keep the one-line edits to the other 13 files that build an `IntrospectionRecord { .. }` literal (status.rs, proposals.rs, evidence_labels.rs, reading.rs, hestia.rs, tests/refusal_corpus.rs, briefs.rs, and cli tests review.rs, proposals.rs, labeled.rs, drain.rs). I grepped `IntrospectionRecord {` over the snapshot and found these literals; each lists every field with no `..` base, so adding any field to the record is a compile error (E0063) in each until it names the new fields. The only edit in each is adding three `Vec::new()` lines inside a test or helper; no behavior, assertion or non-test code in those files changes. This is the same reason labeled.rs is already a deliverable.
decisions.reason: No design for the requirement avoids it: any new record field, one nested field or three, must appear in every full literal. The requirement needs the data on the record, since criterion 3 asserts on the recorded IntrospectionRecord. The extra files are therefore forced by the deliverable, not scope growth.

rejected.option: Add `impl Default` and switch the literals to `..Default::default()`
rejected.why: Still edits every one of the same literals, and adds a Default for a record with required identity fields.

rejected.option: Store the lists in a new record kind or in an existing field (cause, jev)
rejected.why: A new kind needs the allow-list, readers and branch changes in many more places; reusing `cause` changes hestia grouping. Both are larger and break the 'small' default.

rejected.option: Make the fields Option<Vec<String>> to avoid the edit
rejected.why: Option fields are still required in a struct literal; it saves nothing.

risks.risk: Thirteen files outside the expected deliverables hold full IntrospectionRecord literals that stop compiling when fields are added (findings 3-13). Every edit is three `Vec::new()` lines in test or helper code.
risks.mitigation: The edit is mechanical and listed per line in `files`. A missed literal is a compile error (E0063) caught by `cargo clippy --all-targets` and `cargo test --locked`. Step 5 runs `grep -rn 'dropped_ids:' crates` to confirm each site has the new fields beside it. The diff outside the deliverables must show only added `Vec::new()` lines.

risks.risk: The model pads the lists with invented causes or hypotheses, which adds noise to records.
risks.mitigation: The lists are optional, `cause` stays the main cause, an explicit empty list is valid, each list is capped at 5, and the system-prompt sentence says to list only what the input supports. `athena status` does not show them.

risks.risk: The failure path for the new lists is tested through a closure for the reword step, not with a real unrewordable text or a failing redactor; no such input was found by reading.
risks.mitigation: State this in the test description and CHANGELOG. The shared `text` vector means the redaction-failure branch is the same code for all fields; the reword-failure branch is tested through clean_texts.

risks.risk: New apply_answer tests need a working gitleaks binary through the real Redactor, so they fail where it is missing.
risks.mitigation: Both use the existing `athena_with` fixture like the neighbouring apply_answer tests, so they run wherever those run. The data-crate tests (criterion 4) do not need it.

risks.risk: A banned word in new test text trips the xtask boundary scan.
risks.mitigation: All new test strings build banned words from fragments (`["oper", "ator"].concat()`), and the spec and CHANGELOG text avoid the list. `cargo test -p xtask --test policy` is part of `cargo test --locked`.
